A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same OpenVO work. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and supplementary material are readable and support reliable comparison, including content relocated around the reference list.

before.justification: v1 reports original visual-odometry experiments, temporal ablations, latency measurements, oracle evaluations and HD-map reconstruction results.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds component ablations, alternative time-conditioning experiments and additional baseline evaluations.

M1.justification: The proposed temporal conditioning, differentiable 3D flow, geometry encoder and pose decoder remain unchanged. v2 specifies the training loss without establishing that the objective changed. Cross-attention and component removals are evaluated as ablation alternatives.

E1.justification: Both versions retain nuScenes training, KITTI/nuScenes/Argoverse 2 evaluation, varying observation rates, HD-map reconstruction and real-world qualitative examples. The added experiments concern model components and alignment; no additional dataset, domain or task is identified.

E2.justification: v2 Table 10 substantially expands the evaluated comparators with PnP+Metric3Dv2+MaskFlow, DroidCalib and ViPE, adding explicit geometric and optimization-based comparisons. These methods were absent from v1's reported comparisons. The original Table 1 comparator set remains unchanged.

E3.justification: New Table 10 evaluates DroidCalib and ViPE with and without Sim(3) alignment, while Tables 8–9 introduce additional model controls. Section 4.1 clarifies first-frame-only alignment for existing results; this disclosure does not establish that their evaluation procedure changed or that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: v2 adds substantial component validation: cross-attention conditioning with positional encoding versus a scalar time gap (Table 8), and positional-encoding, geometry and flow removal configurations (Table 9). The flow-removed configuration has no numerical results. Table 10 additionally examines alignment sensitivity. Existing temporal, differentiability and oracle analyses are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions disclose seed 2023 and report point estimates. v2 adds no repeated-run counts, additional seed information, confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests.

E6.justification: Tables 1–7 and the HD-map results remain numerically unchanged. New Tables 8–10 substantially expand the results: cross-attention variants have ATEs 155.30 and 180.16, geometry removal gives 158.67, and DroidCalib reports 382.65 without versus 73.18 with Sim(3) alignment. These are additional results under distinct configurations, not improved scores for the retained model. v2 also removes the erroneous prose example labeling 27.38 as Argoverse 2 ATE; Table 4 retains 36.14.

T1.justification: Section 3.3 newly defines the combined translation-MSE and rotation-negative-log-likelihood training objective mathematically. Existing Equations (1)–(18), including the projection, interpolation and differentiability arguments, remain unchanged. No new theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The abstract and introduction retain the same three contributions, calibration-free temporal generalization claim, and reported improvement claims of over 20% and 46%–92%. The shortened conclusion preserves their meaning; new experiments support existing claims rather than redefine them.

C2.justification: New Section 7 discussion explains the time gap as contextual conditioning rather than deterministic pose scaling, and attributes benefits to reduced conflicts between motion scales. It also interprets component dependence and distinguishes aligned from metric-scale comparisons. Existing limitations concerning foundation-prior errors and empirical frequency selection remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 explicitly documents the MSE/NLL loss, ATE units and first-pose alignment with no subsequent SE(3) or Sim(3) alignment. Existing training budgets, hyperparameters, pretrained weights, hardware, runtime information and project URL are retained. These additions improve documentation without demonstrating implementation changes.

R1.justification: v2 adds references and comparison positioning for DroidCalib and ViPE, plus citations connecting the discussion to 3D instance segmentation and object detection. The existing related-work organization and central positioning around temporal awareness and calibration-free VO remain intact.

P1.justification: v2 makes localized wording corrections, shortens the temporal-gap discussion and conclusion, renames Section 5 from Discussion to Conclusion, and adds acknowledgments and Section 7 explanations. References move after the supplementary material. Most original prose and section organization remain unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds three compact tables, renumbers the unchanged HD-map Table 8 as Table 11, reduces Figures 1–2 in size and reflows supplementary displays. Figures 1–9 retain their substantive content. New Table 9 incorrectly repeats Table 8's cross-attention caption despite displaying component ablations.

improvement.justification: v2 improves transparency by specifying the loss and alignment procedure, and strengthens supporting evidence through component ablations and additional baseline comparisons. Existing benchmark results are preserved. However, the new tables do not clearly identify their dataset or sequence subset, and Table 9 has a mismatched caption, limiting interpretability. The net quality gain is useful but modest.
